newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes lose ground, grade prices remain even.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes lose ground, grade prices remain even.

text.p: U.S. crudes started Wednesday weaker, pressured by paper market profit-taking and a slightly bearish take on weekly inventory data.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 15 cents lower at $20.20-30 a barrel, steady with second month July.
Domestic grades moved at a slow pace in the morning, attracting interest from refiners at steady price differentials.
Sweet and sour parcels held their ground from late Tuesday, notably in Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, which had came under renewed pressure on widening WTI/Brent spreads.
